1.title: The Risk Practice
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: The Risk Practice. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the purpose of the risk practice and its relationships with the principles. Explain the purpose of the risk management approach and the risk register. Define risk, risk appetite, risk tolerance, risk cause, event and effect, risk exposure, risk owner, risk action owner, probability and impact. Describe risk planning, analysis, control, culture, decision bias, the recommended response types and the use of data. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Purpose
1.text: Purpose. The risk practice provides a structured way to identify, assess and manage the uncertainties that could affect the project's objectives, so that threats are reduced and opportunities are taken.

1.title: Key concepts
1.text: Key concepts. Risk. A threat or opportunity based on uncertainty: something that might happen and would affect objectives. Risk appetite. The amount of risk an organization is willing to take to reach its objectives. Risk tolerance. The limit of risk exposure that is acceptable at a given level; beyond it, escalate. Risk exposure. The extent to which the project is exposed to the risk's impact.

1.title: Key concepts, continued
1.text: Key concepts. Risk probability. The chance that the risk will happen. Risk impact. The effect on objectives if it does happen. Risk owner. Accountable for managing the risk. Risk action owner. Carries out an action to respond to the risk.

1.title: Cause, event and effect
1.text: Cause, event and effect. A risk is described in three parts: the cause (the situation), the event (what might happen) and the effect (what it would mean for objectives). Exam tip: Risk equals uncertain (might happen). Issue equals has already happened. Risk owner is accountable; action owner does the action. Appetite equals willingness; tolerance equals limit.

1.title: Risk guidance
1.text: Risk guidance. The figure shows this: The risk management steps: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate.

1.title: Risk guidance, continued
1.text: Risk guidance. Risk planning. Agree the approach, roles and scales before the project starts to manage risk. Risk analysis. Identify risks and assess their probability, impact and proximity (when). Risk control. Plan responses, implement them, monitor and communicate. Risk culture. An open, honest environment where people raise risks without blame. Decision bias. Unconscious tendencies (optimism, anchoring) that distort risk judgments; watch for them. Use of data. Use data and tools to analyze and monitor risk. The risk technique has five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate.

1.title: Recommended response types
1.text: Recommended response types. Threats. Avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept, share. Opportunities. Exploit, enhance, share, reject. The wording of the response lists.

1.title: Management products
1.text: Management products. Risk management approach (P I D). How risk is managed on this project: scales, roles, appetite and tolerance. Risk register (project log). A record of identified risks, their owners, assessment and responses. Exam tip: A risk has a cause, event and effect. If a statement says something has happened, it is an issue, not a risk. Exam tip: Threat responses include avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept, share; opportunity responses include exploit, enhance, share, reject. Share appears in both.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A supplier might deliver late, which would delay testing. Which term describes this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A risk. It might happen, so it is a risk; an issue has already happened.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) A risk can be a threat or an opportunity. (two) A risk owner is accountable for managing the risk. (three) A risk action owner is accountable for the risk. (four) A risk is something that has already happened. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one and two. Risks are threats or opportunities, and the risk owner is accountable.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. Risk blank is the amount of risk an organization is willing to take to reach its objectives. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Appetite. That is risk appetite.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. The team decides to buy insurance so another party bears the financial impact. Which threat response is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Transfer. Moving the impact to another party is transfer.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. The team chooses to exploit an opportunity. Which statement fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: It tries to make the opportunity definitely happen. Exploit makes sure the opportunity is realized.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Where is the list of identified risks, owners and responses recorded? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The risk register. The risk register records risks and responses.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define a risk. Answer: A threat or opportunity based on uncertainty. Question two. What are the three parts of a risk description? Answer: Cause, event and effect. Question three. What is risk tolerance? Answer: The limit of risk exposure acceptable at a given level.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the threat responses. Answer: Avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept and share. Question five. Name the opportunity responses. Answer: Exploit, enhance, share and reject. Question six. Name the five steps of the risk technique. Answer: Identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Risk: threat or opportunity from uncertainty (cause, event, effect). Appetite or tolerance: willingness or limit. Owners: risk owner accountable; action owner acts. Threat responses: avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept, share. Opportunity responses: exploit, enhance, share, reject. Products: risk management approach, risk register.
